benefits.title: King’s student offer is tested against external relevance rather than internal assumption
benefits.statement: Interventions, opportunities, skills priorities and relevant curriculum or near-curriculum developments are exposed to structured employer, alumni, professional and sector challenge, giving King’s stronger evidence about what should be sustained, strengthened, changed or investigated further.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, faculties, departments and King’s Edge delivery teams
benefits.owner: Andrew Wright with relevant King’s Edge and faculty leads
benefits.realisationPeriod: From Year 1 pilots, becoming systematic across 2027/28 and 2028/29
benefits.successLooksLike: Priority student interventions and opportunities can show how appropriate external insight has informed their design, validation or subsequent development, with material recommendations tracked to a response.

benefits.title: Graduate premium and reputational claims have stronger external credibility
benefits.statement: King’s can distinguish between claims that are internally evidenced and claims that are also recognised and substantiated by employers, alumni, professions, sectors and other relevant external communities.
benefits.beneficiary: King’s, faculties, departments, prospective and current students, and teams using graduate premium assets
benefits.owner: Rachel Kershaw and Andrew Wright with 2.4.1 and 2.4.4 leads
benefits.realisationPeriod: From the first validation cycle, deepening as the 2.4.1 asset estate grows
benefits.successLooksLike: Priority graduate premium propositions and reputational outputs record the external evidence or validation that supports them, and claims that do not withstand challenge are refined, qualified or withdrawn.

benefits.title: External insight becomes a coherent institutional intelligence system
benefits.statement: University, faculty and departmental employer and alumni insight structures operate to a shared minimum standard, making local intelligence more useful while reducing duplication, identifying gaps and allowing important themes to aggregate into an institutional view.
benefits.beneficiary: University, faculty and departmental leaders and external-engagement communities
benefits.owner: Andrew Wright with Careers, alumni and faculty or departmental panel leads
benefits.realisationPeriod: Model established in 2026/27, broader adoption in 2027/28, embedded by 2028/29
benefits.successLooksLike: King’s can map its external insight coverage, show consistent expectations across levels, produce an annual synthesis of material external intelligence and trace significant recommendations through to named institutional responses.
